news.headline: US-Iran Conflict Keeps Oil Elevated at $90–96/bbl
news.what_happened: US and Israel military operations against Iran since February 28 have collapsed Iranian oil exports by 1–1.4 mbd. WTI rose 0.56% to $90.72; Brent near $95. Trump overnight played down prolonged conflict, giving slight relief.
news.why_it_matters: Crude at $90+ pressures airlines, paints, tyres and logistics sectors in India. Benefits ONGC and OMCs via higher realization and inventory gains. Every $10 Brent rise adds ~₹8,000 Cr to ONGC's annual profit.

news.headline: FII Net Buying Surges to ₹6,688 Cr — Highest in Weeks
news.what_happened: Foreign institutional investors bought ₹6,688 Cr net in the cash segment on September 2; DIIs added ₹2,813 Cr. FIIs simultaneously hold 2,29,163 contracts short in index futures as a hedge.
news.why_it_matters: Massive FII inflow confirms risk-on stance for India. Large-cap Nifty 50 stocks — especially banks and IT — are primary beneficiaries. Futures short is a hedge, not a bearish call on individual stocks.

news.headline: US Markets Rebound — S&P 500 +0.5%, Nasdaq +0.5%, Nvidia +3%
news.what_happened: Wall Street snapped a three-day losing streak on Sep 2. S&P 500 closed at 7,666.60 (+0.5%), Dow at 53,061.95 (+0.6%), Nasdaq at 26,217.83 (+0.5%). Nvidia surged 3% leading tech.
news.why_it_matters: Positive global cue supports Indian IT and broader market at open. When Nasdaq rises 0.5%+, Indian IT sector typically opens 0.5–1% higher. Risk-on makes FIIs more constructive on Indian equities.

news.headline: Rupee at ₹94.98 — Weak Currency Lifts IT & Pharma Exporters
news.what_happened: USD/INR settled near 94.98, with the rupee weakening on oil import pressure and capital flows. Intraday low of 94.40 on Sep 2; high of 95.61 last week.
news.why_it_matters: IT and pharma export companies earn in USD. At ₹95/dollar versus ₹83–84 two years ago, exporters receive ~13–15% more INR per dollar of revenue — a direct P&L uplift each quarter.

news.headline: Gold at $4,360 — Safe Havens Bid on US-Iran + Fed Hike Risk
news.what_happened: Gold recovered to $4,360/oz from a near one-month low, supported by geopolitical uncertainty and the US 10Y yield at 4.79% (5-session high). Markets now price a 66% chance of a Fed rate hike in September.
news.why_it_matters: Higher gold prices elevate collateral values for gold loan NBFCs (MUTHOOTFIN, MANAPPURAM), boosting their loan book without credit risk increase. Fed hike probability is a headwind for rate-sensitive sectors globally.

picks.catalyst: Nasdaq +0.5% overnight + USD/INR at 94.98 (rupee weak, dual tailwind)
picks.logic: TCS earns ~85% revenue in USD and other foreign currencies. At USD/INR 95 versus ₹83–84 two years ago, every dollar of revenue translates to ~13–15% more INR — a direct quarterly P&L uplift. Nasdaq recovery signals IT sector multiple expansion globally. FII inflow of ₹6,688 Cr positions TCS as a prime destination. Watch zone based on Sep 2 close of ₹2,343 (avg of 2,338–2,348).

picks.catalyst: FII net buying ₹6,688 Cr (multi-week high) + US markets +0.5% + GIFT Nifty +0.47%
picks.logic: HDFCBANK is the single largest constituent of FII portfolios in Indian equities. When FIIs buy in this size, HDFCBANK receives the largest allocation. US banking stocks rose with the S&P 500, providing global valuation support. As the largest Nifty private bank by weight, any index-level buying flows through HDFCBANK first. Watch zone based on Sep 2 close of ₹700.80.
